models.inverse_notes: Target w1: known w0>0 and f<1 give w1=w0*(1-f)>0, unique. Target w0: known w1>0,f<1 give w0=w1/(1-f)>0, unique; denominator exclusion is f!=1 and positivity strengthens it to f<1. Retain original contexts. Check f=0.05,w0=80 gives w1=76 kg and forward f=0.05; f=-0.05,w0=60 gives w1=63 and forward -0.05. At f=0, one known positive mass uniquely determines the equal other. f=1 would require zero current mass and is excluded; f alone without either mass leaves infinitely many positive pairs when f<1. No biological causal inverse is asserted.
limitations: Body-mass change alone does not distinguish tissue, fluid, edema, dehydration or other components; the source cautions that these affect nutritional interpretation.
No malnutrition threshold, desired change, intervention or monitoring schedule is encoded. A usual mass obtained by recall rather than measurement needs its own uncertainty metadata.

models.inverse_notes: Target w1: known w0>0,t>0 and r give w1=w0+r*t, requiring w1>0. Target w0: known w1>0,t>0 and r give w0=w1-r*t>0. Target t: known endpoint masses and r!=0 give t=(w1-w0)/r; require t>0, so change and rate must have the same sign. Retain original guards/context. Check r=1.1574074074074074e-6 kg/s,w0=60,t=1728000 s gives w1=62 and forward r matches. For r=0 and w1=w0, any t>0 fits; for r=0 and unequal masses none fits. Equal masses with r!=0 would give t=0 and are excluded. These inverses do not establish a physiological causal law.
limitations: Endpoint mean may hide nonlinear growth or fluctuation and does not separate tissue, water or measurement error.
No interval adequacy, target gain, age-based threshold, feeding decision or monitoring protocol is supplied; measurement uncertainty can dominate small endpoint changes.

references.method: Independent synthetic interval partition: a total 2 kg increase across 20 equal 24-hour days corresponds to 0.1 kg/day. Convert that counted mean once to kg/s; t=20*86400 s. This is an average, not a claimed daily trajectory. Tolerance is arithmetic only.
A signed 3 kg decrease over 30 equal days corresponds to -0.1 kg/day, normalized to kg/s. Materially different sign and interval; no linear within-interval loss assumed.
Equal positive endpoint masses have zero net mean change over a positive day, without proving the instantaneous mass remained constant.

rejection_cases.reason: Two endpoints with zero elapsed interval cannot define this mean rate.
Elapsed interval is missing; visit count or nominal month is not substituted.

relationship.translation_notes: Introduced w1 and w0 map to present and initial mass; introduced t is the positive elapsed interval corresponding to the source day difference, normalized to seconds. r is kg/s rather than kg/day; day conversion belongs to unit scales (86400 s for a continuous 24-hour day), not an inlined equation factor. Dimensions (M-M)/T=M T^-1; kg's numerical scale applies equally to the input masses and output rate, so the expression is canonical. The endpoint definition gives a time average; no constant instantaneous growth assumption is introduced. It is not a separately minted inverse of postpartum mass retention because it defines a generic time-normalized quantity with a supplied interval and no pregnancy-specific baseline.

models.inverse_notes: Target B: known R>=0,C>0 give B=R*C uniquely. Target C: known B>0,R>0 give C=B/R>0. Retain original serum/analyte contexts. B>0,R=0 has no finite solution; B=0,R>0 would imply C=0 and violates the denominator domain. These are laboratory-ratio algebraic views, not clearance inversions or clinical inferences.

relationship.translation_notes: Introduced C maps to eClcr, a to age's numerical value in years, w to weight, and sCr to SCr. Introduced z is 0 for the source male branch or 1 for its female branch; 1-0.15*z exactly encodes the published 15% reduction, not a fitted continuous sex factor. Age is a numerical year index (unit years, dimensionless in this snapshot), not an elapsed-time input converted to seconds. Serum creatinine is kg/m^3, so 1 mg/dL=0.01 kg/m^3. The source denominator coefficient 72 kg*min*dL/(mg*mL) becomes 432000000000 s in coherent units. With w in the runtime mass base and sCr on the same mass scale, mass cancels and C is m^3/s. Dimensions: (1)*(1)*M/(T*(M L^-3))=L^3 T^-1. The normalized 432000000000 is the dimensional empirical coefficient, not an extra input/output unit conversion. Unit scales alone must convert future mL/min display ports. Unambiguous NKF extracted equation is the authority; original PDF visual inspection was unavailable, so no full-original methods/table inspection is claimed.
